input.rationale: Successor experiment for the wedge investigation that measures the margin generalization recorded with it. The harness is unchanged for the three-voter cases and now also runs the same staging on five voters in both the control and the faulted mode, removing healthy voters one at a time and applying a client entry after each removal, so the step at which commit stops can be compared between the control and the wedged cluster. Native local feedback in a scratch copy inside draft showed the control committing after two removals while the faulted five-voter cluster committed after one removal and stalled at the second, but the retained execution decides.

scope.description: Five subtests share one harness: control and injected_store_error on three voters with one escalation step, injected_store_error_then_restart on three voters, and control_five_voters and injected_store_error_five_voters on five voters with two escalation steps. Each case builds the cluster from the library's own in-memory components with a legal fault-injecting LogStore wrapper on the node that becomes the initial leader, runs the partition/divergence/higher-term-replacement history, heals, samples the certificate and store for 1500 ms, removes the fault and samples once more, then removes one healthy voter per step (disconnecting it in both directions) and applies one client entry per step while recording the leader's commit index over 1500 ms, whether that apply future completes, its error, and the leader's and the wedged node's probes with every node's state and term.
assumptions: Removing a healthy voter at the transport level models that voter failing; the remaining voters keep their membership in the configuration, so the quorum size stays the configuration's quorum.
The wedged replica stays connected in every step, because it must keep receiving the leader's retries for the margin claim to be about the wedge rather than about an unreachable node.
A LogStore returning an error from StoreLogs is an allowed outcome of the interface, and the wrapper returns it without touching the underlying store.
The control and faulted five-voter cases differ only in whether that one StoreLogs call returned an error.
excluded: No production code is modified and no fault other than the single store error is injected.
No restart, snapshot install or leader-side compaction is exercised in this experiment; the restart path is covered by the earlier receipt.

experiment.prefix: Each subtest prints the CA_EVENT lines described before; peer_loss_after_wedge now carries mode, step, voters (the configuration size), removed_voter, leader, leader_state, leader_term, commit_before, commit_samples over 1500 ms, apply_future_done, apply_future_error, leader_probe, wedged_node_probe and state_and_term.
experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation and staging, with the voter count and the number of escalation steps parameterized so that five-voter control and faulted cases run the same legal partition/divergence/higher-term replacement history and then lose healthy voters one at a time; the earlier receipts remain the witnesses for the three-voter windows and the restart path.

scope.description: Two cases in one execution, both driving the public API of the unmodified library in-process with the package's in-memory transport, stores and snapshot store. Case A (control): MakeCluster(3) with default protocol version 3, then LeadershipTransferToServer to a voter. Case B: MakeCluster(3) plus a separate MakeClusterNoBootstrap(1) merged and fully connected, then AddNonvoter for that node, wait until the non-voter has learned the 4-server configuration and caught up to a freshly committed proof entry, then LeadershipTransferToServer to that non-voter. Each case records the leader's configuration with suffrages, the future's error and duration, the target's and incumbent's state and term, timestamped state sampling for 500 ms, the observer stream of RequestVoteRequests (candidate id, term, log position, transfer flag), and whether the voters hold one leader again afterwards.
assumptions: In-memory LoopbackTransport delivers RPCs in-process without loss, so any nonprogress or state change observed is produced by the library's own logic rather than by a transport fault.
inmemConfig timeouts (heartbeat/election/lease 50 ms, commit 5 ms) make election and recovery observable inside a short window.
The non-voter's membership and catch-up are established through the library's own producers: AddNonvoter plus a committed proof entry the target has applied.
Protocol version 3 is the default, which is required for both AddNonvoter and LeadershipTransferToServer.
excluded: No production function is modified, wrapped or re-implemented; only the public API and the library's observer/testing facilities are used.
No artificial clock, timeout injection or fault injection is used.

basis.prefix: Each test prints CA_EVENT JSON lines. Control case: control_transfer_before / control_transfer_after. Non-voter case: nonvoter_transfer_before / nonvoter_transfer_after / nonvoter_transfer_recovery. RequestVoteRequest observations carry candidate_id, term, transfer_flagged; sampled_transitions carries t_ms, node, state, term.

scope.description: Two subtests run the same legal history, differing only in whether the node's store fails the StoreLogs call that follows a conflicting-suffix deletion. Each case builds three voters with NewInmemTransport, NewInmemStore (wrapped by a legal fault-injecting LogStore implementing the interface), NewInmemSnapshotStore and the package MockFSM, bootstrapped with the library's BootstrapCluster and started with NewRaft. The initial leader is then isolated at the transport level, keeps two Apply calls in its own log, the other two nodes elect a leader at a higher term and commit two entries, and the partition is healed. The case records: the diverging node's cached certificate (getLastEntry), its reported LastIndex, commit and applied indexes, the wrapped store's FirstIndex/LastIndex and whether GetLog of the certificate index errors, and the store's StoreLogs attempt/delivery counters, sampled every 25 ms for 1500 ms after the heal and once more 1200 ms after the fault (if any) is removed. The leader's own certificate and store counters are recorded alongside.
assumptions: A LogStore returning an error from StoreLogs is an allowed outcome of the interface, not corruption of an acknowledged durable write; the wrapper returns such an error without touching the underlying store.

The staged history is a legal single-cluster history: the diverging node's tail entries were appended while it was partitioned and therefore uncommitted, and the majority's replacement entries are committed at a higher term.
In-memory LoopbackTransport delivers RPCs in-process without loss, so nonprogress is produced by the library's logic rather than by transport faults.
The fault is armed only on the diverging node and only after the majority has committed its replacement entries, so the failing call is the StoreLogs that follows the conflicting-suffix deletion.
excluded: No production code is modified; the wrapper implements the public LogStore interface only.
No snapshot install, restart or leader-side compaction is performed, so the question of whether those repair the state stays open in this execution.

basis.prefix: Each case prints CA_EVENT JSON lines: truncation_before_heal (the two nodes' probes before the partition heals), truncation_after_heal (probes plus the 1500 ms sampling arrays cert_index_samples, store_last_samples, store_attempts), and truncation_after_disarm (a probe 1200 ms after the fault is removed). Probes carry cert_last_index/cert_last_term, reported_last, commit_index, applied_index, store_first/store_last, store_attempts/store_delivered and cert_entry_error.

scope.description: Two subtests, absent_server and control_present_server. Each starts a one-voter cluster with MakeCluster(1), records the leader, its state, term, last index and the configuration, then calls the public AddVoter on the leader for a second server whose address comes from a fresh in-memory transport. In the absent case that transport is unwired and no raft runs on it; in the control the named server's raft is created and both transports are connected before the call. Each case then samples every 25 ms for 1500 ms: the original node's state, term, commit index and last index, whether the AddVoter future has completed and with what error, and whether the config entry index (recorded last index plus one) is committed. Afterwards a bounded client write is attempted, then the named server is started (in the absent case) and both cases record whether the configuration commits and a leader exists again within 4 s.
assumptions: Bootstrap a single voter and grow it with AddVoter is the sequence BootstrapCluster's documentation recommends, so the staged input follows the library's own guidance rather than an invented operator error.
The named server's identity and address are well formed (the ID is the address-derived ID of protocol version 3), and only its availability differs between the two cases.
In-memory LoopbackTransport delivers RPCs in-process without loss, so a refused RPC means the peer was not wired, not that a network fault intervened.
excluded: No production code is modified and no fault is injected.
No snapshot, restart or manual recovery path is exercised; the recovery observation only brings the named server up.

basis.prefix: Each subtest prints CA_EVENT lines: growth_before (leader, state, term, commit and last index, configuration, named server identity and whether it is up, and the expected configuration entry index), growth_window (sampled state, term, commit and last index arrays, how many samples saw a Leader, whether the AddVoter future completed and its error, plus final values and whether the configuration entry committed), growth_write_attempt (the error of a bounded client write) and growth_recovery (whether the configuration committed and a leader exists after the named server is started, with the nodes' states and the elapsed time).

scope.description: Three subtests: control, injected_store_error and injected_store_error_then_restart, each building three voters from the library's own in-memory components with a legal fault-injecting LogStore wrapper, running the legal partition/divergence/higher-term-replacement history, healing, sampling the certificate and store for 1500 ms, then removing the fault and sampling once more after 1200 ms. The restart subtest then shuts the node down (which closes its transport), creates a fresh transport at the same address, rewires the peers to it, starts NewRaft on the same log store, stable store and snapshot store, and records getLastEntry, store LastIndex, commit index, the store counters and the full probe for up to four seconds (20 samples at 200 ms) together with whether the certificate index equals the store's last index.
assumptions: A restart is modelled as the library itself performs it at startup: a new raft instance over the same durable state (log store and stable store), after Shutdown has closed the previous transport.
NewRaft rebuilds the configuration by rescanning the log entries from the last snapshot index, so the restarted node knows the configuration the leader holds.
The leader's replication goroutine keeps the peer's next index from the wedge phase; after the restart it re-sends the entries that were previously rejected.
In-memory LoopbackTransport has a 500 ms RPC timeout, so a call in flight when the transport closed fails and the replication retries afterwards; the four-second window covers that.
excluded: No production code is modified; the restart uses NewRaft on the same durable state only.
No InstallSnapshot path is exercised, and no leader-side compaction is reached.

basis.prefix: The three subtests print the CA_EVENT lines described before, plus truncation_after_restart for the third: converged (certificate index equals the store's last index), cert_samples and store_last_samples and commit_samples over four seconds, the full diverging probe, and elapsed_ms.

scope.description: Two subtests, absent_server and control_present_server. Each starts a one-voter cluster with MakeCluster(1), records the leader, its state, term, last index and the configuration, then calls the public AddVoter on the leader for a second server whose address comes from a fresh in-memory transport. In the absent case that transport is unwired and no raft runs on it; in the control the named server's raft is created and both transports are connected before the call. Each case then samples every 25 ms for 1500 ms: the original node's state, term, commit index and last index, whether the AddVoter future has completed and with what error, and whether the config entry index (recorded last index plus one) is committed. Afterwards a bounded client write is attempted, then the named server is started (in the absent case) and both cases record whether the configuration commits and a leader exists again within 4 s.
assumptions: Bootstrap a single voter and grow it with AddVoter is the sequence BootstrapCluster's documentation recommends, so the staged input follows the library's own guidance rather than an invented operator error.
The named server's identity and address are well formed (the ID is the address-derived ID of protocol version 3), and only its availability differs between the two cases.
In-memory LoopbackTransport delivers RPCs in-process without loss, so a refused RPC means the peer was not wired, not that a network fault intervened.
excluded: No production code is modified and no fault is injected.
No snapshot, restart or manual recovery path is exercised; the recovery observation only brings the named server up.

basis.prefix: Each subtest prints CA_EVENT lines: growth_before (leader, state, term, commit and last index, configuration, named server identity and whether it is up, and the expected configuration entry index), growth_window (sampled state, term, commit and last index arrays, how many samples saw a Leader, whether the AddVoter future completed and its error, plus final values and whether the configuration entry committed), growth_write_attempt (the error of a bounded client write) and growth_recovery (whether the configuration committed and a leader exists after the named server is started, with the nodes' states and the elapsed time).

scope.description: Three subtests: control, injected_store_error and injected_store_error_then_restart, each building three voters from the library's own in-memory components with a legal fault-injecting LogStore wrapper, running the legal partition/divergence/higher-term-replacement history, healing, sampling the certificate and store for 1500 ms, then removing the fault and sampling once more after 1200 ms. The restart subtest then shuts the node down (which closes its transport), creates a fresh transport at the same address, rewires the peers to it, starts NewRaft on the same log store, stable store and snapshot store, and records getLastEntry, store LastIndex, commit index, the store counters and the full probe for up to four seconds (20 samples at 200 ms) together with whether the certificate index equals the store's last index.
assumptions: A restart is modelled as the library itself performs it at startup: a new raft instance over the same durable state (log store and stable store), after Shutdown has closed the previous transport.
NewRaft rebuilds the configuration by rescanning the log entries from the last snapshot index, so the restarted node knows the configuration the leader holds.
The leader's replication goroutine keeps the peer's next index from the wedge phase; after the restart it re-sends the entries that were previously rejected.
In-memory LoopbackTransport has a 500 ms RPC timeout, so a call in flight when the transport closed fails and the replication retries afterwards; the four-second window covers that.
excluded: No production code is modified; the restart uses NewRaft on the same durable state only.
No InstallSnapshot path is exercised, and no leader-side compaction is reached.

basis.prefix: The three subtests print the CA_EVENT lines described before, plus truncation_after_restart for the third: converged (certificate index equals the store's last index), cert_samples and store_last_samples and commit_samples over four seconds, the full diverging probe, and elapsed_ms.

before.description: Two subtests, control and injected_store_error, each building three voters from the library's own in-memory components with a legal fault-injecting LogStore wrapper on the node that becomes the initial leader, running the legal partition/divergence/higher-term-replacement history, healing, sampling the certificate and store for 1500 ms, removing the fault and sampling once more after 1200 ms. Then the escalation phase, identical in both subtests: the current leader is located, the remaining healthy voter is disconnected in both directions, one client entry is applied on the leader, and for 1500 ms the leader's commit index, whether the returned future completes, its error, the leader's and the wedged node's certificate/store probes and every node's state and term are recorded.
assumptions: A LogStore returning an error from StoreLogs is an allowed outcome of the interface, not corruption of an acknowledged durable write; the wrapper returns the error without touching the underlying store.

The staged history is a legal single-cluster history: the tail entries the diverging node holds were appended while it was isolated and were never committed, and the majority's replacement entries are committed at a higher term.
Three voters with one removed is the failure the configuration is expected to tolerate, so a stalled commit in that state is meaningful rather than an artifact of the setup.
In-memory LoopbackTransport delivers RPCs in-process without loss, so nonprogress is produced by the library's logic rather than by transport faults.
excluded: No production code is modified; the wrapper implements the public LogStore interface only.
No restart, snapshot install or leader-side compaction is performed, so those repair paths remain unexecuted in this experiment.

scope.description: Five subtests share one harness: control and injected_store_error on three voters with one escalation step, injected_store_error_then_restart on three voters, and control_five_voters and injected_store_error_five_voters on five voters with two escalation steps. Each case builds the cluster from the library's own in-memory components with a legal fault-injecting LogStore wrapper on the node that becomes the initial leader, runs the partition/divergence/higher-term-replacement history, heals, samples the certificate and store for 1500 ms, removes the fault and samples once more, then removes one healthy voter per step (disconnecting it in both directions) and applies one client entry per step while recording the leader's commit index over 1500 ms, whether that apply future completes, its error, and the leader's and the wedged node's probes with every node's state and term.
assumptions: Removing a healthy voter at the transport level models that voter failing; the remaining voters keep their membership in the configuration, so the quorum size stays the configuration's quorum.
The wedged replica stays connected in every step, because it must keep receiving the leader's retries for the margin claim to be about the wedge rather than about an unreachable node.
A LogStore returning an error from StoreLogs is an allowed outcome of the interface, and the wrapper returns it without touching the underlying store.
The control and faulted five-voter cases differ only in whether that one StoreLogs call returned an error.
excluded: No production code is modified and no fault other than the single store error is injected.
No restart, snapshot install or leader-side compaction is exercised in this experiment; the restart path is covered by the earlier receipt.
